reason: The text repeatedly establishes the Hebrews' primary religious identity and devotion to Yahweh. Moses and Aaron identify themselves and their people as followers of 'the God of the Hebrews' (אֱלֹהֵ֣י הָֽעִבְרִ֔ים). Throughout the narrative, the Hebrews' foremost concern and stated purpose is to worship and sacrifice to Yahweh in the wilderness (וְנִזְבְּחָה֙ לַֽיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ). The entire passage frames their central identity around their covenant relationship with Yahweh—they are willing to endure Egyptian oppression and hardship specifically in order to fulfill their religious obligation to serve Him. Their statements consistently emphasize this as their paramount identity and purpose.
